results.title: KBO to hand out MVP, top rookie awards Nov. 26
results.content: The top baseball league announced Friday it will hold its annual awards ceremony next week in Seoul, to be highlighted by the regular-season MVP award and the top rookie prize. The Korea Baseball Organization (KBO) said the annual KBO Awards ceremony will take place at 2 p.m. next Thursday at Lotte Hotel World in Seoul. The KBO announced 14 candidates for the MVP award on Oct. 13, with leaders of major pitching and hitting categories earning automatic nominations. Nine players earned nominations for the Rookie of the Year. Those who had not accumulated 30 innings or 60 plate appearances over the past five years qualified as rookies, except those who had played pro ball overseas before coming to the KBO. results.title: Man referred to prosecution on suspicion of killing teen victim of son's alleged sex crime
results.content: Police on Friday referred a man to the prosecution on suspicion of killing a teenage girl alleged to have been sexually assaulted by his son, officials said. The 59-year-old was referred to the Seoul Northern District Prosecutors Office, according to the Seoul Seongbuk Police Station. During questioning, the suspect said he killed the teenager on impulse out of anger while asking her to submit a written statement saying she did not wish for his son to be punished, the police said. Police placed the man under emergency arrest last week after finding the female victim dead at a house listed on Airbnb in Seoul's northeastern Seongbuk Ward. He was reportedly drunk at the time of his arrest. The victim's parents had filed a complaint in March against the murder suspect's son, accusing him of having sexual relations with their daughter in January. results.title: HD Hyundai Heavy hosts US maritime delegation at Ulsan shipyard
results.content: HD Hyundai Heavy Industries said Friday a U.S. maritime delegation visited its shipyard to discuss cooperation in shipbuilding, military logistics and port infrastructure. The delegation, led by Mark D. Johnson, deputy administrator of the U.S. Maritime Administration (MARAD), toured the shipyard in Ulsan, about 360 kilometers southeast of Seoul, on Thursday. MARAD, an agency under the U.S. Department of Transportation, oversees maritime transport of military supplies during national emergencies and supports port infrastructure development. The visit came as Washington pushes to rebuild its domestic shipbuilding industry under its "Bridge Strategy," which seeks to leverage the shipbuilding expertise and production capacity of allies while expanding its own industrial base. results.title: Heroes bring back 3 foreign players from 2026 season, acquire new Japanese pitcher
results.content: The Kiwoom Heroes completed their foreign player signings Friday, as they re-signed three players for another season and acquired a new Japanese pitcher to fill their Asian quota. The Heroes said pitcher Raul Alcantara, infielder Matt Davidson and outfielder Keston Hiura all agreed to new one-year contracts. Former Nippon Professional Baseball (NPB) pitcher Koji Fukutani will be the Heroes' new Asian quota player, replacing closer Yuto Kanakubo. In the Korea Baseball Organization (KBO), clubs can each sign three non-Asian foreign players, with a maximum two pitchers. They typically carry two foreign pitchers and one position player. The Heroes were the only team in 2026 to end the year with one pitcher and two position players with Alcantara, Davidson and Hiura. results.title: Dubai eyes closer ties with Korea on AI in logistics, mobility: official
results.content: Dubai sees potential for closer cooperation with Korea on the use of artificial intelligence (AI) in logistics and mobility, a senior official at the Dubai Future Foundation has said. Khalifa Al Qama, the think tank's chief of research, made the remarks during a press session on Thursday when asked which areas Korea and Dubai should prioritize as AI use expands. "We think this is a very exciting time to invest even more into enabling people to find new solutions by deploying technologies like AI towards sectors," Al Qama said. "And when it comes to Korea and Dubai, we have a good ecosystem when it comes to trade and logistics, moving things from the east to the west," he said. Trade plays a major role in the economies of both Korea and Dubai. Al Qama said such cooperation could draw on Dubai's expertise in operating airports and seaports. results.title: Lee Kang-in named top Asian footballer overseas for 2nd straight year
results.content: Lee Kang-in of Atletico Madrid has become the first back-to-back winner of an award recognizing the top Asian football player in foreign competitions. Lee, a South Korean national team mainstay, was named the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) Asian International Player of the Year at the AFC Awards ceremony Thursday in Bangkok. The annual award is given to the Asian player with the best performance outside the continent. Lee beat out fellow South Korean Hwang In-beom and Japanese player Ayase Ueda. Lee is the first consecutive winner of his prize since its introduction in 2012 and is the second multiple winner after his compatriot Son Heung-min, who claimed it in 2015, 2017, 2019 and 2023. Lee picked up five trophies during the 2025-2026 season with Paris Saint-Germain, including his third straight French Ligue 1 title and second straight UEFA Champions League trophy. results.title: Hyundai Motor unveils new Elantra, Genesis G80 Hybrid at LA Auto Show
results.content: Hyundai Motor said Friday it has unveiled its eighth-generation Avante compact sedan, known as the Elantra in North America, and the Genesis G80 Hybrid at the Los Angeles Auto Show. The Korean automaker showcased the all-new 2027 Elantra and 2028 Elantra Hybrid during a media preview of the auto show at the Los Angeles Convention Center in California. The all-new Elantra will be available with two powertrain options: a 2.0-liter gasoline engine and a 1.6-liter hybrid powertrain. Genesis, Hyundai Motor's luxury brand, also unveiled the G80 Hybrid with enhanced power output and fuel efficiency. The G80 Hybrid combines a 2.5-liter turbocharged gasoline engine with a dual-motor hybrid system, offering a driving range of approximately 1,029 kilometers on a single tank of fuel. results.title: Seoul subway union launches 'work-to-rule' campaign over hiring, wage dispute
results.content: Unionized workers at Seoul Metro launched a "work-to-rule" campaign Friday as they remain locked in a dispute with management over hiring and wages. Under the collective action that began at 6 a.m., participants will fully adhere to safety regulations, such as maintaining train speeds regardless of subway schedules, in a move expected to slow down operations. The union plans to continue the collective action and launch an indefinite strike next Wednesday unless the management responds to its demands for an additional hiring of 1,313 personnel and a wage increase of 3.5 percent. It has also called for the management to scrap a plan to cut 2,212 jobs. Unionized workers of Korea Railroad Corp. (KORAIL) have also warned of launching an indefinite general strike on Dec. 10, demanding the hiring of more safety-related personnel.

results.title: Seoul shares open sharply lower tracking US losses after Anthropic debut
results.content: Seoul shares opened sharply lower Friday, tracking losses on Wall Street, as Anthropic's solid market debut failed to ease concerns over whether heavy investment in artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure will generate returns. After opening 4.08 percent lower, the benchmark Korea Composite Stock Price Index (KOSPI) fell 183.50 points, or 3.57 percent, to 4,954.39 as of 9:15 a.m. Overnight, the Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 2.19 percent, and the tech-heavy Nasdaq composite declined 2.25 percent. Investors are awaiting further evidence that heavy investment in the AI sector will generate sustainable returns, despite Anthropic's successful market debut. Shares in Anthropic soared 17 percent above their initial public offering (IPO) price of $83 to close at $97.17 on Thursday (U.S. time) on Wall Street. results.title: Unification minister set to hold 1st talks with US top envoy, USFK chief
results.content: Unification Minister Chung Dong-young was set to meet U.S. Ambassador Michelle Steel and U.S. Forces Korea (USFK) Commander Gen. Xavier Brunson on Friday, the ministry said. It will be Chung's first official meeting with Steel, who arrived here in late July as Washington's top envoy to Seoul. The ministry confirmed last month that it was arranging the meeting. Since her arrival, Steel has met a series of South Korean ministers, beginning with Foreign Minister Cho Hyun in early August. That she had yet to meet Chung more than two months into her tenure, however, had fueled speculation that the United States was displeased with Chung's alleged leak of classified information on North Korea. The speculation centered on Chung's remarks in March about a third uranium enrichment facility in North Korea, which the U.S. government regards as classified information. results.title: N. Korea, Laos vow deeper cooperation in Pyongyang meeting
results.content: Officials from North Korea and Laos have met in Pyongyang to discuss measures to expand cooperation in the economy, trade, and science and technology sectors, Pyongyang's state media reported Friday. The fourth session of the joint committee on economic, trade, scientific and technological cooperation was held at the Pyongyang Assembly Hall on Thursday, the Korean Central News Agency (KCNA) said. Yun Jong-ho, the North's external economic relations minister, led the country's delegation, while Malaithong Kommasith, Laos' industry and commerce minister, headed that of Laos. The two sides "discussed in detail the practical items of bilateral cooperation" in those areas and signed a protocol at the end of the session, the report said. results.title: Foreigners continue to offload Korean stocks in Oct.
results.content: Foreign investors continued to sell Korean stocks in October amid extended geopolitical risks and woes over artificial intelligence (AI) profitability, data showed Friday. Offshore investors offloaded a net 25.97 trillion won ($19.49 billion) worth of local stocks last month compared with a net selling of 19.11 trillion won the previous month, according to the data from the Financial Supervisory Service (FSS). Following their net selling in October, offshore investors owned 1,899 trillion won worth of local stocks, or 34 percent of total market capitalization. By country, investors from the United States were the top sellers in October by selling a net 15.9 trillion won, followed by Asian countries with 5.6 trillion won of selling, the latest findings showed. results.title: Producer prices drop in Oct. on lower food prices
results.content: Producer prices fell for the first time in three months in October, driven by lower prices of agricultural goods on mild weather conditions, central bank data showed Friday. The producer price index (PPI), a key gauge of future consumer inflation, dropped 0.1 percent last month from a month earlier, following a 0.1 percent on-month gain each in August and September, according to the preliminary data from the Bank of Korea (BOK). The index had risen for 10 consecutive months since September 2025 and fell in July. From a year earlier, producer prices rose 7.2 percent in October, slowing from the previous month's 7.6 percent on-year gain, the latest findings showed. Producer prices are a key indicator of future inflation trends, as they influence the prices businesses charge consumers in the months ahead. results.title: China exposure set to widen profit gap among Korean tire makers
results.content: Korea’s three tire makers — Hankook Tire, Kumho Tire and Nexen Tire — are set to see their European profit margins come under pressure, as the European Union (EU) tightens trade barriers on tires manufactured in China as early as next month. The EU is expected to finalize countervailing duties on Chinese-made tires in early December, posing an additional financial burden to Korean tire makers after the EU started imposing anti-dumping duties from July. If finalized as currently proposed, the combined tariff rate on tires made at Chinese plants and exported to Europe will rise to 28.76 percent both for Kumho Tire and Nexen Tire, and 27.5 percent for Hankook Tire. The impact will vary widely because the three companies rely on Chinese plants to different degrees for their European sales. results.title: [WEEKENDER] Next chapter of Korean instant noodles: Beyond Buldak
results.content: Global consumer hits such as Buldak and Shin Ramyun have demonstrated new possibilities for Korean instant noodles, showing that products once thought to be only for Korean consumers can whet appetites overseas as well. As demand for their products surges outside Korea, reflected in rising export volumes, food companies are beginning to reorganize their production bases and product portfolios to sustain the momentum and cater to global consumers. Their strategies center on two main goals: expanding production capacity and offering a wider range of products beyond the intensely spicy varieties that have helped drive their global popularity. Samyang Foods, which introduced Buldak in 2012, expects to complete and begin operating its new manufacturing plant in Jiaxing, Zhejiang province, China, by the end of this year. results.content: Experts warned that the two-state approach gaining ground in both Koreas could entrench the peninsula’s division, calling instead for a unification strategy focused on freedom and human rights for North Koreans, backed by deterrence and the alliance with the United States. results.title: Omnichannel fuels Olive Young's bet on AI
results.content: Beauty retail giant CJ Olive Young on Thursday said it will further develop its online platform into an omnichannel service that more effectively connects its products to global consumers, making shopping more convenient both in Korea and overseas. Chief Operating Officer Lee Jin-hee said the company, established in 1999, is now leading the growing global commerce trend that integrates online and offline channels into a singular marketplace, thereby enabling the company to serve 18 million members and the massive influx of foreign visitors to Korea while meeting their expectations. “It’s a digitally unified commerce, satisfying both online and offline shopping,” Lee said during a press conference in Seoul. “From social media to fintech and retail platforms, everything is now merging at e-commerce. results.title: Beyond apologies: Korean adoptees, families renew calls for government accountability
results.content: Overseas Korean adoptees, Korean birth families and civil society organizations gathered outside Cheong Wa Dae in Seoul Oct. 30, calling on the government to address decades of human rights violations and family separations linked to intercountry adoption. The press conference brought together overseas adoptee organizations and Korean advocacy groups in a united effort to seek accountability for past adoption practices and their lasting consequences for both adoptees sent abroad and families who remained in Korea. The gathering came more than a year after President Lee Jae Myung apologized to overseas adoptees and their birth families in October 2025, following the findings by the Truth and Reconciliation Commission (TRC) of systemic human rights violations in Korea's overseas adoption practices. results.title: Trump says he will meet with N.Korea's Kim Jong Un 'at some point', NBC reports
results.content: U.S. President Donald Trump said in an interview with NBC on Thursday that he could not meet North Korea's Kim Jong Un during his Asia trip because he had too many meetings, but added that two would meet "at some point." "The relationship is there, but we didn't meet," Trump was quoted as saying by an NBC News reporter on X. "There was too many meetings...It wouldn't have worked out…We'll have that meeting at some point," Trump added.

results.title: S. Korean firm plans $150 million lifeline for Eric Trump-backed robot maker
results.content: NEW YORK — South Korean conglomerate Base Group is preparing to invest $150 million in a struggling military-robot maker backed by U.S. President Donald Trump's son Eric, internal company emails show, deepening the firm’s ties to the Trump family that have already drawn congressional scrutiny.
